1.1: Sha’ul, an emissary - not from men, nor by a man, but by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ and Elohim the Father who raised Him from the dead -
1.2: and all the brothers who are with me, to the assemblies of Galatia:
1.3: Favor to you and peace from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Father and our Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ,
1.4: who gave Himself for our sins, to deliver us out of this present wicked age, according to the desire of our Elohim and Father,
1.5: to whom be the praise forever and ever. Amĕn.
1.6: I marvel that you are so readily turning away from Him who called you in the favor of Mashiaḥ, to a different ‘good news,’
1.7: which is not another, only there are some who are troubling you and wanting to corrupt the Good News of Mashiaḥ.
1.8: However, even if we, or a messenger out of the shamayim, bring a ‘good news’ to you beside what we announced to you, let him be accursed.
1.9: As we have said before, and now I say again, if anyone brings a ‘good news’ to you beside what you have received, let him be accursed.
1.10: For do I now persuade men, or Elohim? Or do I seek to please men? For if I still pleased men, I should not be a servant of Mashiaḥ.
1.11: And I make known to you, brothers, that the Good News announced by me is not according to man.
1.12: For I did not receive it from man, nor was I taught it, but through a revelation of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ.
1.13: For you have heard of my former behavior in Yahuḏaism, how intensely I persecuted the assembly of Elohim, and ravaged it.
1.14: And I progressed in Yahuḏaism beyond many of my age in my race, being more exceedingly ardent for the traditions of my fathers.
1.15: But when it pleased Elohim, who separated me from my mother’s womb and called me by His favor,
1.16: to reveal His Bĕn in me, that I might bring Him, the Good News, to the gentiles, I did not immediately consult with flesh and blood,
1.17: neither did I go up to Yerushalayim, to those who were emissaries before me. But I went to Araḇia, and returned again to Dammeseq.
1.18: Then after three years I went up to Yerushalayim to learn from Kĕpha, and remained with him for fifteen days.
1.19: And I saw no other of the emissaries except Ya’aqoḇ, the brother of the Aḏon.
1.20: And what I write to you, see, before Elohim, I do not lie.
1.21: Then I went into the districts of Suria and of Kilikia.
1.22: And I was not known by sight to the assemblies of Yahuḏah which were in Mashiaḥ,
1.23: but they were hearing only that, “The one who once persecuted us now brings as Good News the belief which he once ravaged.”
1.24: So they were esteeming Elohim in me.

2.1: Then after fourteen years I again went up to Yerushalayim, with Barnaḇah, taking Titos along too.
2.2: And I went up by revelation, and laid before them that Good News which I proclaim among the gentiles, but separately to those who were esteemed, lest somehow I run, or had run, in vain.
2.3: But not even Titos who was with me, though a Yawanite, was compelled to be circumcised.
2.4: But because of the false brothers, sneakingly brought in, who sneaked in to spy out our freedom which we have in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 in order to enslave us,
2.5: to these we did not yield in subjection, not even for an hour, so that the truth of the Good News remains with you.
2.6: But from those who were esteemed to be whatever - what they were, it makes no difference to me, Elohim shows no partiality - for those who were esteemed contributed naught to me.
2.7: But on the contrary, when they saw that the Good News to the uncircumcised had been entrusted to me, even as Kĕpha to the circumcised -
2.8: for He who worked in Kĕpha to make him an emissary to the circumcised also worked in me for the gentiles.
2.9: So when Ya’aqoḇ, Kĕpha, and Yoḥanan, who seemed to be supports, came to know the favor that had been given to me, they gave me and Barnaḇah the right hand of fellowship, with purpose of we unto the gentiles and they to the circumcised,
2.10: only that we might remember the poor, which I myself was eager to do.
2.11: And when Kĕpha had come to Antioḵeia, I withstood him to his face, because he was at fault.
2.12: For before some came from Ya’aqoḇ, he was eating with the gentiles, but when they came, he began to withdraw and separate himself, in fear of those of the circumcision.
2.13: And the rest of the Yahuḏim joined him in hypocrisy, so that even Barnaḇah was led away by their hypocrisy.
2.14: But when I saw that they are not walking straight according to the truth of the Good News, I said to Kĕpha before them all, “If you, being a Yahuḏi, live as a gentile and not as the Yahuḏim, why do you compel gentiles to live as Yahuḏim?
2.15: “We, Yahuḏim by nature, and not of the gentiles, sinners,
2.16: knowing that a man is not declared right by works of Torah, but through belief in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, even we have believed in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, in order to be declared right by belief in Mashiaḥ and not by works of Torah, because by works of Torah no flesh shall be declared right.
2.17: “And if, while seeking to be declared right by Mashiaḥ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is Mashiaḥ then a servant of sin? Let it not be!
2.18: “For if I rebuild what I overthrew, I establish myself a transgressor.
2.19: “For through Torah I died to Torah, in order to live to Elohim.
2.20: “I have been impaled with Mashiaḥ, and I no longer live, but Mashiaḥ lives in me. And that which I now live in the flesh I live by belief in the Bĕn of Elohim, who loved me and gave Himself for me.
2.21: “I do not put aside the favor of Elohim, for if righteousness is through Torah, then Mashiaḥ died for naught.”

3.1: O senseless Galatiyim! Who has put you under a spell, not to obey the truth - before whose eyes 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ was clearly portrayed among you as impaled?
3.2: This only I want to learn from you: Did you receive the Ruaḥ by works of Torah, or by the hearing of belief?
3.3: Are you so senseless? Having begun in the Ruaḥ, do you now end in the flesh?
3.4: Have you suffered so much in vain - if indeed in vain?
3.5: Is He, then, who is supplying the Ruaḥ to you and working miracles among you, doing it by works of Torah, or by hearing of belief?
3.6: Even so Aḇraham “believed Elohim, and it was reckoned unto him as righteousness.”
3.7: Know, then, that those who are of belief are sons of Aḇraham.
3.8: And the Scripture, having foreseen that Elohim would declare right the nations by belief, announced the Good News to Aḇraham beforehand, saying, “All the nations shall be given beraḵah in you,”
3.9: so that those who are of belief receive beraḵah with Aḇraham, the believer.
3.10: For as many as are of works of Torah are under the curse, for it has been written, “Cursed is everyone who does not continue in all that has been written in the Book of the Torah, to do them.”
3.11: And that no one is declared right by Torah before Elohim is clear, for “The righteous shall live by belief.”
3.12: And the Torah is not of belief, but “The man who does them shall live by them.”
3.13: Mashiaḥ redeemed us from the curse of the Torah, having become a curse for us - for it has been written, “Cursed is everyone who hangs upon a tree.”
3.14: in order that the beraḵah of Aḇraham might come upon the nations in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, so that we might receive the promise of the Ruaḥ through belief.
3.15: Brothers, as a man I say it: a Covenant, even though it is man’s, yet if it is confirmed, no one puts it aside, or adds to it.
3.16: But the promises were spoken to Aḇraham, and to his Seed. He does not say, “And to seeds,” as of many, but as of One, “And to your Seed,” who is Mashiaḥ.
3.17: Now this I say, Torah, that came four hundred and thirty years later, does not annul a Covenant previously confirmed by Elohim in Mashiaḥ, so as to do away with the promise.
3.18: For if the inheritance is by Torah, it is no longer by promise, but Elohim gave it to Aḇraham through a promise.
3.19: Why, then, the Torah? It was added because of transgressions, until the Seed should come to whom the promise was made. And it was ordained through messengers in the hand of a mediator.
3.20: The Mediator, however, is not of one, but Elohim is One.
3.21: Is the Torah then against the promises of Elohim? Let it not be! For if a law had been given that was able to make alive, truly righteousness would have been by Torah.
3.22: But the Scripture has shut up all under sin, that the promise by belief in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ might be given to those who believe.
3.23: But before belief came, we were being guarded under Torah, having been shut up for the belief being about to be revealed.
3.24: Therefore the Torah became our trainer unto Mashiaḥ, in order that we might be declared right by belief.
3.25: And after belief has come, we are no longer under a trainer.
3.26: For you are all sons of Elohim through belief in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
3.27: For as many of you as were immersed into Mashiaḥ have put on Mashiaḥ.
3.28: There is not Yahuḏi nor Yawanite, there is not slave nor free, there is not male and female, for you are all one in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
3.29: And if you are of Mashiaḥ, then you are seed of Aḇraham, and heirs according to promise.

4.1: And I say, for as long as the heir is a child, he is no different from a slave, though he is master of all,
4.2: but is under guardians and trustees till the time prearranged by the father.
4.3: So we also, when we were children, were under the elementary matters of the world, being enslaved.
4.4: But when the completion of the time came, Elohim sent forth His Bĕn, born of a woman, born under Torah,
4.5: to redeem those who were under Torah, in order that we might receive the adoption as sons.
4.6: And because you are sons, Elohim has sent forth the Ruaḥ of His Bĕn into your hearts, crying, “Abba, Father!”
4.7: So you are no longer a slave but a son, and if a son, also an heir of Elohim through Mashiaḥ.
4.8: But then, indeed, not knowing Elohim, you served those which by nature are not mighty ones.
4.9: But now after you have known Elohim, or rather are known by Elohim, how do you turn again to the weak and poor elementary matters, to which you want to be enslaved again?
4.10: You closely observe days and months and seasons and years.
4.11: I fear for you, lest by any means I have labored for you in vain.
4.12: Brothers, I beg you to become as I am, because I am as you are. You did not wrong me at all.
4.13: But you know that through weakness of the flesh I brought the Good News to you before.
4.14: And my trial which was in my flesh you did not despise or reject, but you received me as a messenger of Elohim, as Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
4.15: What then was your joy? For I bear you witness, that if possible, you would have plucked out your own eyes and given them to me.
4.16: So then, have I become your enemy, speaking truth to you?
4.17: They are ardent towards you, for no good, but they want to shut you out, that you might be ardent towards them.
4.18: And it is good always to be ardent in what is good, and not only when I am present with you.
4.19: My little children, for whom I am again in birth pains until Mashiaḥ is formed in you,
4.20: and I want to be present with you now and to change my voice, for I have doubts about you.
4.21: Say to me, you who want to be under Torah, do you not hear the Torah?
4.22: For it has been written that Aḇraham had two sons, one by a female servant, the other by a free woman.
4.23: But he who was of the female servant was born according to the flesh, and he of the free woman through promise.
4.24: This is allegorical, for these are the two covenants: one indeed from Mount Sinai which brings forth slavery, which is Haḡar,
4.25: for this Haḡar is Mount Sinai in Araḇia, and corresponds to Yerushalayim which now is, and is in slavery with her children.
4.26: But the Yerushalayim above is free, which is the mother of us all.
4.27: For it has been written, “Rejoice, O barren, you who do not bear! Break forth and shout, you who do not have birth pains! For the deserted one has many more children than she who has a husband.”
4.28: And we, brothers, as Yitsḥaq was, are children of promise.
4.29: But, as he who was born according to the flesh then persecuted him who is according to the Ruaḥ, so also now.
4.30: But what does the Scripture say? “Cast out the female servant and her son, for the son of the female servant shall by no means be heir with the son of the free woman.”
4.31: Therefore, brothers, we are not children of the female servant but of the free woman.

5.1: In the freedom with which Mashiaḥ has made us free, stand firm, then, and do not again be held with a yoke of slavery.
5.2: See, I, Sha’ul, say to you that if you become circumcised, Mashiaḥ shall be of no use to you.
5.3: And I witness again to every man being circumcised that he is a debtor to do the entire Torah.
5.4: You who are declared right by Torah have severed yourselves from Mashiaḥ, you have fallen from favor.
5.5: For we, in Ruaḥ, by belief, eagerly wait for the expectation of righteousness.
5.6: For in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any strength, but belief working through love.
5.7: You were running well, who held you back from obeying the truth?
5.8: That persuasion does not come from Him who calls you.
5.9: A little leaven leavens all the lump.
5.10: I trust in you, in the Aḏon, that you shall have no other mind. And he who is troubling you shall bear his judgment, whoever he is.
5.11: And I, brothers, if I still proclaim circumcision, why am I still persecuted? Then the stumbling-block of the stake has been put aside.
5.12: O that those who disturb you would even cut themselves off!
5.13: For you, brothers, have been called to freedom, only do not use freedom as an occasion for the flesh, but through love serve one another.
5.14: For the entire Torah is completed in one word, in this, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.”
5.15: And if you bite and devour one another, beware lest you be consumed by one another!
5.16: And I say: Walk in the Ruaḥ, and you shall not accomplish the lust of the flesh.
5.17: For the flesh lusts against the Ruaḥ, and the Ruaḥ against the flesh. And these are opposed to each other, so that you do not do what you desire to do.
5.18: But if you are led by the Ruaḥ, you are not under Torah.
5.19: And the works of the flesh are well-known, which are: adultery, whoring, uncleanness, indecency,
5.20: idolatry, drug sorcery, hatred, quarrels, jealousies, fits of rage, selfish ambitions, dissensions, factions,
5.21: envy, murders, drunkenness, wild parties, and the like - of which I forewarn you, even as I also said before, that those who practice such as these shall not inherit the Malḵuth of Elohim.
5.22: But the fruit of the Ruaḥ is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, trustworthiness,
5.23: gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no Torah.
5.24: And those who are of Mashiaḥ have impaled the flesh with its passions and the desires.
5.25: If we live in the Ruaḥ, let us also walk in the Ruaḥ.
5.26: Let us not become conceited, provoking one another, envying one another.

6.1: Brothers, if a man is overtaken in some trespass, you the spiritual ones, put such a one straight in a spirit of meekness, looking at yourself lest you be tried too.
6.2: Bear one another’s burdens, and so complete the Torah of Mashiaḥ.
6.3: For if anyone thinks himself to be somebody, when he is not, he deceives himself.
6.4: But let each one examine his own work, and then he shall have boasting in himself alone, and not in another.
6.5: For each one shall bear his own burden.
6.6: And let him who is instructed in the Word share in all that is good, with him who is instructing.
6.7: Do not be led astray: Elohim is not mocked, for whatever a man sows, that he shall also reap.
6.8: Because he who sows to his own flesh shall reap corruption from the flesh, but he who sows to the Ruaḥ shall reap everlasting ḥai from the Ruaḥ.
6.9: And let us not lose heart in doing good, for in due season we shall reap if we do not grow weary.
6.10: So then, as we have occasion, let us do good to all, especially to those who are of the household of the belief.
6.11: See with what big letters I have written to you with my own hand!
6.12: As many as want to make a good show in the flesh, these compel you to be circumcised, only so that they should not be persecuted for the stake of Mashiaḥ.
6.13: For those who are circumcised do not even watch over the Torah, but they want to have you circumcised so that they might boast in your flesh.
6.14: And for me, let it not be that I should boast except in the stake of our Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, through whom the world has been impaled to me, and I to the world.
6.15: For in Mashiaḥ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 neither circumcision nor uncircumcision has any strength, but a renewed creature.
6.16: And as many as walk according to this rule, peace and compassion be upon them, and upon the Yisra’ĕl of Elohim.
6.17: From now on let no one trouble me, for I bear in my body the scars of the Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
6.18: The favor of our Aḏon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ be with your spirit, brothers. Amĕn
